newsitem.title: USA: Leaders meet Clinton in joint session.
newsitem.headline: Leaders meet Clinton in joint session.

text.p: Leaders of Israel, the Palestinians and Jordan met with President Bill Clinton at the White House on Tuesday for a group Middle East crisis summit.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Jordan's King Hussein gathered in the Oval Office with Clinton and Vice President Al Gore for what was expected to be a meeting of more than an hour, the White House said.
Clinton said the summit symbolised "our commitment to end the violence and get the peace process going again."

"We're going to work today. We're going to work tomorrow," the U.S. president told reporters during a picture-taking session at the start of the group meeting. Also present were Vice President Al Gore, Secretary of State Warren Christopher and U.S. National Security Adviser Anthony Lake.

Clinton earlier met separately with Netanyahu and Arafat to open his planned two-day effort to rescue the foundering Middle East peace process from collapse after an outburst of Israeli-Palestinian violence last week.
The mood of the meeting was sombre. Arafat and Netanyahu sat on couches facing each other. King Hussein sat next to Clinton in an armchair.
